name: RED STATIC: Pirate Neural Broadcast Collective
creator: Founding cell unknown; publicly associated with 'the Kassem-Varga node'
description: Red Static is the most technically sophisticated pirate neural feed operation in GLMZ, capable of momentarily hijacking licensed broadcast channels to insert unauthorized content before corponation countermeasures can locate and sever the signal. Its broadcasts range from political agitprop and leaked corporate documents to underground art, music, and the occasional raw unedited security footage from inside corponation facilities. Broadcasts last between ninety seconds and twelve minutes — long enough to matter, short enough to evade trace. The collective's membership is unknown; its aesthetic is unmistakable: a red static burst, then silence, then the content.
medium: neural feed (pirate channel injection), legacy video hijack
cultural_impact: Red Static's interruptions have become a cultural event — when the red burst appears, people record and redistribute the content through physical media before it can be scrubbed from licensed channels, creating a distributed archive that enforcement agencies have been unable to fully suppress.
controversy: Red Static is classified as a Tier One Broadcast Security Threat by the Meridian Corponation Compliance Authority; possession of Red Static content is technically an offense under the Unauthorized Information Distribution Act, a law so broadly applied to Red Static archives that enforcement has become selectively targeted rather than universal — which critics argue is itself a form of social control.
story_hooks: Red Static has broadcast what appears to be genuine footage from inside a corponation detention facility — and the people visible in the footage include someone who was officially reported dead two years ago.

The Kassem-Varga node has gone silent for three weeks; competing theories hold that the collective was captured, went deep underground voluntarily, or was co-opted — and someone is still broadcasting using their signature red burst.

A character receives a physical chip containing the next Red Static broadcast before it airs, along with a note asking them to decide whether it should be released — the content is explosive enough to trigger serious violence, and the collective wants someone outside their cell to make the call.
